answer: In the agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each participant to lock a refundable bond in a shared staking pool for at least one epoch. An attacker wanting to flood the system with fake identities must acquire and lock real capital for every one, facing opportunity cost and slash risk if peers detect collusion. This raises the barrier far above mere key generation. Even across the frozen tundra of low-activity periods, the echo of honest behavior persists as the tide of new agents brings fresh capital that dilutes any concentrated attack.
